expectations.text: The tutor reads the learner's existing local state (course/syllabus) before answering, instead of inventing course/exam details from nothing.
expectations.evidence: Transcript steps 3-4 run `status` (after an initial Git-Bash backslash-path failure, retried successfully with forward slashes), returning real workspace state: course.exam (date 2026-09-18, delivery oral, question_model ticket_list), session state, review_queue, and per-ticket mastery for all 6 tickets. Step 6 lists the actual `.exam-prep/` state files (course.json, syllabus.json, learner.json, etc.) confirming this is persisted state, not fabricated. Step 7 reads syllabus.json to get ticket-3's real title ('Теорема Лагранжа о среднем значении') and metadata. Step 8 reads learner.json for stored preferences. The final reply's claims (ticket availability, exam format matching 'no problems') are traceable to this real data, not invented.

expectations.text: The tutor follows the ticket_list track order: asks for a brief answer structure (which theorem, hypotheses/conclusion or formula meaning, shape of the argument) as its own step, separate from and before requesting/giving the full statement or proof.
expectations.evidence: Final reply (outputs/final_reply.md) asks exactly three brief-structure questions before anything else: (1) one-sentence statement of what the theorem asserts, (2) hypotheses and conclusion, (3) the 1-2 sentence shape/skeleton of the proof and what construction it relies on. It explicitly defers the next stage: 'После этого перейдём к полной формулировке и доказательству целиком, а затем — к проверке на понимание' (only after this do we move to the full statement/proof, then comprehension check). This matches references/pedagogy.md's ticket_list stage order and its explicit instruction not to collapse 'give me ticket N' into 'recite it in full'.

expectations.text: The tutor does NOT introduce a practice-problem, worked-example, or 'let's solve a problem together' stage for this ticket — no problem is invented where the syllabus and exam format have none.
expectations.evidence: The reply contains no problem, example, or exercise. It explicitly frames the mode as ticket recitation rather than problem-solving: '...тренируемся именно в режиме «рассказать билет», а не «решить пример»' (we practice in 'recite the ticket' mode, not 'solve an example' mode).

expectations.text: The tutor asks the learner to attempt/recite before evaluating or revealing the full theorem and proof, rather than immediately reciting the theorem itself.
expectations.evidence: The reply never states the theorem's content, hypotheses, conclusion, or proof. It only names the ticket's title (from syllabus.json) and then asks the learner to answer the three brief-structure questions 'по памяти, без подглядывания' (from memory, without looking it up) before anything is revealed.

expectations.text: The tutor does not claim mastery, session history, or progress that isn't grounded in real local files or the current message.
expectations.evidence: The only status-like claims in the reply ('доступен без незакрытых предпосылок' / available with no open prerequisites) are directly grounded in the real `status` output (ticket-3 availability: 'available', prerequisites: [] in syllabus.json). No claim of prior mastery, no fabricated session history, no invented progress; the transcript's own reasoning (step 4) explicitly notes 'nothing has been attempted yet ... there is no prior evidence to report back about ticket-3 specifically.'

expectations.text: The reply engages with the learner's actual ticket 3 (Теорема Лагранжа о среднем значении, as defined in their own syllabus), rather than asking the learner to supply the ticket's content or substituting a generic unrelated theorem.
expectations.evidence: syllabus.json (step 7) defines ticket-3's title as 'Теорема Лагранжа о среднем значении', and the final reply opens with exactly that: 'Билет 3 — «Теорема Лагранжа о среднем значении»'. The tutor does not ask the learner what ticket 3 is about and does not substitute a different theorem.

suggestions.assertion: The tutor does NOT introduce a practice-problem, worked-example, or 'let's solve a problem together' stage for this ticket — no problem is invented where the syllabus and exam format have none.
suggestions.reason: The learner's own message already states 'никаких задач на экзамене не будет' (no problems will be on the exam). A baseline tutor with no skill at all would very likely honor this explicit instruction by default, since it requires no read of local state or pedagogy logic to avoid inventing a problem here — it just requires not contradicting what the user said. This assertion doesn't strongly discriminate a skilled response from an unskilled one on this particular prompt.

suggestions.assertion: The tutor does not claim mastery, session history, or progress that isn't grounded in real local files or the current message.
suggestions.reason: Most competent baseline assistants avoid fabricating mastery/history claims by default (general anti-hallucination behavior), especially when the user's message gives no history to hallucinate about. This assertion is closer to a generic 'don't make things up' check than a specific test of the skill's local-state-grounding behavior; expectation 1 already covers the more discriminating version of this (did it actually go read the local state at all).

suggestions.assertion: The tutor asks the learner to attempt/recite before evaluating or revealing the full theorem and proof, rather than immediately reciting the theorem itself.
suggestions.reason: This substantially overlaps with the ticket_list-track-order assertion (expectation 2) and is also a fairly common default 'Socratic tutor' instinct independent of this skill's specific pedagogy.md stage sequence — many baseline tutoring prompts already ask learners to try first before being told the answer. Consider merging this into expectation 2 or sharpening it to require the specific *brief-structure* checkpoint (not just 'ask before revealing' in general) to make it more discriminating.

eval_feedback.overall: All 6 expectations pass on genuine, well-grounded evidence (real local-state reads driving the specific ticket-3 content and the pedagogy.md-mandated stage sequence), so this is not a rubber-stamp pass. However, three of the six assertions (problem-avoidance, no-false-mastery-claims, attempt-before-reveal) would likely also be satisfied by a reasonably competent tutor with no access to this skill at all, given how directly the learner's own message states the exam format. The strongest, most discriminating assertions here are #1 (actually reading local course/syllabus state) and #2 (following the specific brief-structure-then-full-answer stage split from pedagogy.md) and #6 (surfacing the real ticket-3 title from syllabus.json rather than a generic theorem) — these would clearly fail for an unskilled baseline that either invents course details or jumps straight to reciting a theorem. No assertion currently checks whether the tutor honors the learner's stored preferences (learner.json: concise style, delay_full_solution) in its actual reply style/length, which was observed to hold here but goes untested.
